## Basic age, count data!  
\  

```{r}
# Pabna District, mid year 2022 (illustrative figures)
age_group <- c("0-4",   "5-9",   "10-14", "15-19", "20-24",
               "25-29", "30-34", "35-39", "40-44", "45-49",
               "50-54", "55-59", "60-64", "65-69", "70-74",
               "75-79", "80+")

male   <- c(124500, 138200, 142300, 131400, 118200,
            104500, 96300,  88700,  78400,  67100,
            56800,  47200,  38500,  28700,  19600,
            11400,  8200)

female <- c(119800, 132400, 136700, 128900, 122600,
            110800, 102400, 94200,  82500,  70200,
            58900,  48400,  39200,  29800,  21200,
            13500,  11800)

pop <- data.frame(age_group, male, female)
head(pop)
```

## Male Population Ratio

```{r}
male <- sum(pop$male)
total = sum(pop$female) + male
MP = (male/total) * 100
sprintf("The male population ratio is %.2f%%", MP)
```
There are 49 men in every 100 people.

```{r}
pop$total <- pop$male + pop$female

# Population by broad age band
P_0_14  <- sum(pop$total[1:3])     # rows 1, 2, 3 = ages 0 to 14
P_15_64 <- sum(pop$total[4:13])    # rows 4 to 13 = ages 15 to 64
P_65    <- sum(pop$total[14:17])   # rows 14 to 17 = ages 65 and over

ACR <- P_65 / P_0_14 * 100
sprintf("The AGED CHILD RATIO is %.2f%%\n", ACR)
```

There are 18 old people or each 100 children of age 0-14.

```{r}
TDR  <- (P_0_14 + P_65) / P_15_64 * 100
CDR  <- P_0_14            / P_15_64 * 100
OADR <- P_65              / P_15_64 * 100

round(c(Total = TDR, Child = CDR, OldAge = OADR), 2)
```
There are 55 people dependent on every 100 independent people.

## New Data

```{r, results='asis'}
age_group <- c("0-4","5-9","10-14","15-19","20-24","25-29",
               "30-34","35-39","40-44","45-49","50-54","55-59",
               "60-64","65-69","70-74","75-79","80+")
male   <- c(196500,213400,218700,198500,168300,142800,128400,
            114700,98300,82600,67800,54300,42800,31200,21400,
            12700,8900)
female <- c(188200,204800,209300,192400,178500,152400,138600,
            121200,102800,85400,70200,56800,44500,32800,23500,
            14800,12200)

syl <- data.frame(age_group, male, female)

M <- sum(syl$male)    # 1,801,300
F <- sum(syl$female)  # 1,828,400

round(M / (M + F) * 100, 2)  # MP ≈ 49.62
round(M / F * 100, 2)        # SR ≈ 98.52
```
There are 49 men in every 100 people.
There are 98 men for every 100 females.

```{r}
syl$total <- syl$male + syl$female

P_0_14 <- sum(syl$total[1:3])     # 1,230,900
P_65   <- sum(syl$total[14:17])   # 157,500

ACR <- P_65 / P_0_14 * 100
round(ACR, 2)   # ≈ 12.80

```
There are 12 old people for every 100 children of age 0-14
```{r}
sum(syl$female[5:8])
```

There are 590700 women of age 20-39.
```{r}
P_15_64 <- sum(syl$total[4:13]) 

TDR  <- (P_0_14 + P_65) / P_15_64 * 100
CDR  <- P_0_14            / P_15_64 * 100
OADR <- P_65              / P_15_64 * 100

round(c(Total = TDR, Child = CDR, OldAge = OADR), 2)

all.equal(TDR, CDR + OADR)   
```
There are 62 dependent people for every 100 independent people.


```{r}
M <- sum(syl$male)
F <- sum(syl$female)
M - F
M - (102 / 100) * F
```
We need 27100 more males to balance the population.
And we will need 63668 more males for the target (102 males for every 100 females)


```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Reshape data into long format
pop_long <- pop %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(male, female), names_to = "gender", values_to = "population") %>%
  mutate(population = ifelse(gender == "male", -population, population))

# Plot
ggplot(pop_long, aes(x = age_group, y = population, fill = gender)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.9) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_labels_custom <- scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(-150000, 150000, 50000),
    labels = function(x) abs(x)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Pabna District, 2022", x = "Age Group", y = "Population") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("male" = "#2563eb", "female" = "#f472b6")) +
  theme_minimal()
```
